Use a fictional in-museum itinerary to link the material, the times, the visitor questions and the temporary closure information. Being able to explain the basis for a change has more observational value than memorising a florid commentary.

The experience is an editorial design, not a tour guide qualification examination, a recruitment assessment or real tour leading; an occupational interest result does not prove practising qualifications or service ability.

Being willing to check exhibit labels, practise a concise explanation and take in feedback can serve as a signal for further exploration; the specific tasks and qualification requirements still need checking.
If you are unwilling to explain repeatedly, keep walking and standing, or handle on-site changes, check the job setting first; do not give a personality diagnosis from one experience.
Complete G1 to G3 on paper, record the specific process of correcting errors, scheduling and responding to feedback, then choose one real role to check the conditions.

This occupation handles visit guidance, location commentary and responding to visitor questions; themed venue tours and attraction visit services may have different procedures. Travel agency operation, overall event planning and historical research are other responsibilities, and they are not merged just because they all serve visitors.

Read the confirmed location material, the group requirements and the itinerary conditions first, separating facts, interpretation and unknowns. The G1 exhibit label clearly states 1912, so the 1888 in the commentary draft is not used as the documentary basis.

The commentary should serve the visitors' understanding: from the exhibit label fact to a clear explanation, then responding to questions. The editorial experience can record a short explanation and the unknown questions, without filling the gaps with sentimentality or invented stories.

After receiving a venue update, check the route and the times and keep a record of the changes. When G2 closes B, only the prompt-confirmed alternative C may be used, and other unconfirmed halls must not be treated as available.

The same commentary can adjust its expression and pace for different groups, but the facts, venue rules and available routes must be re-checked. Repeated tours do not mean the hall status and visitor needs are always the same.

Communicate updates and visitor needs with the venue, the travel agency, the driver and the relevant colleagues. The commentary task does not automatically authorise driving, first aid or any contract change, and questions go to the corresponding person for verification.

The work may involve part-time, peak-season and irregular hours, and the specific role requires checking the scheduling, preparation time, transport and pay; a historical recruitment only helps read the conditions and does not mean applications are still open.

Afterwards, hand over the questions and the change records under the actual process, and organise the approved commentary work; visitor personal information and unauthorised photographs are not made public just because someone joined a tour.

Themed venue tours centre on the location material and the visit route, while attraction visit services need to fit the itinerary and the group arrangements. The process below is an editorial task structure, and the real contract, venue rules and assignment are checked separately.
Themed venue tour
Check the exhibit label and the object → arrange the stops and times → rehearse and re-check → explain and answer questions → receive material updates → complete records and handover
Sourced commentary points, a checkable route and a record of questions
Attraction visit service
Check the assignment and the itinerary → check the location and requirements → confirm the assembly arrangements → guide and explain → report and confirm changes → re-check records and close out
Completing the visit service under the confirmed arrangements and handing over the necessary changes
Shared task foundation
Material verification · language expression · listening to questions · time coordination · explaining the rules · re-checking updates
How are themed venue tours and attraction visit services distinguished?

The two directions share guidance and commentary; the venue one centres more on exhibits or a fixed location, while the attraction service needs to fit the group itinerary and transport arrangements. This is an editorial task summary and does not give the roles a uniform qualification classification.
Service purpose
Helping visitors understand specific exhibits, a site or a theme.
Helping a group complete a visit to an attraction under the confirmed arrangements and obtain the relevant information.
Main inputs
Exhibit labels, venue-confirmed material, opening status and visitor questions.
The assignment and itinerary, location material, assembly and transport, and group requirements.
Task process
Check the theme and the facts, arrange the stops, explain and answer questions, and receive venue updates.
Check the itinerary and the assembly arrangements, organise the visit, and communicate and re-check promptly when a change is found.
Checkable outputs
An accurate and concise explanation, the route times and a record of unresolved questions.
The visit service provided under the confirmed arrangements, and the handover of questions and changes.
Scope of responsibility
The guide checks the material and communicates with visitors; opening, venue facilities and professional judgements are confirmed by the corresponding staff.
Chinese tour guide services are checked against the actual practice and assignment requirements, and a guide may not privately take on business or alter the itinerary without authorisation.
How they cooperate
Check the exhibit labels, closure information, rules and group pace with the venue staff.
Communicate the itinerary and anomalies with the travel agency, the venue and the transport staff, without crossing professional boundaries.
Different boundaries
A venue commentary title does not automatically determine Chinese tour guide legal status and must be judged by the actual activity.
The combined United States Tour Guides and Travel Guides statistic does not mean an independent wage for every role in this occupation, or Chinese pay.
Which checkable judgements does the on-site tour require?

Whether the material is reliable, whether the group understands, whether the time and route are usable and who confirms a change are observable questions in the editorial experience; real risks and professional handling follow the on-site process separately.
Do the dates in the commentary match the exhibit label?
Does the statement separate known material, interpretation and the unknown?
Can the visit finish on time after a closure or route update?
Does the feedback ask to change the fact, the expression or the arrangement?

First turn the feedback into a checkable object. In G2, feedback one corrects the date and admits the unknown, and feedback two adjusts the confirmed alternative route after the closure; show the basis before and after each change.
Is there the corresponding authority for driving, first aid or a paid change?

The tour task does not automatically grant a professional qualification or contract change authority. Check the real personnel, training, assignment and rules, and do not operate a vehicle, provide medical care or charge fees on the basis of a paper practice.
At the end, which questions and material need to be handed over?

Preparation｜verifying location material｜Check the original source of the exhibit label and the historical or environmental material, and separate confirmed from to-be-checked, without treating a draft as original fact.

Arranging｜route and visit pace｜Arrange the stops together with the confirmed opening status and the group's needs, list the times and the unknowns, and check the specific route against the actual rules.

Communicating｜commentary and responding to questions｜Explain the key points of the location and listen carefully to the visitors' questions; when unclear, register them truthfully and ask the corresponding person to confirm.

Service｜guidance and explaining the rules｜Organise the visit, explain the assembly and the points to note, and observe visitor activity, without crossing professional and authorisation boundaries in a service capacity.

Updating｜re-checking and reporting changes｜After receiving a closure, weather or itinerary update, check the impact and communicate the adjustment under the actual process, avoiding unauthorised changes.

Handover｜questions and material maintenance｜Organise the unresolved questions, the changes and the service feedback, keep the material according to its use, and ensure the work does not leak visitor information or invent experience.
Section title｜Where and how do tour guides and escorts work?

The work may take place indoors or outdoors at venues, historical sites or attractions, often in direct contact with the public and requiring commentary, walking between stops and coordination. The actual environment varies with the role and the group.

Common locations｜Museums, public buildings, historical sites and attractions, among others; a venue tour and an outbound escort differ, and the work location, transport and opening conditions are confirmed by the task.

Materials and tools｜Location material, exhibit labels, routes, schedules and group requirements are the inputs; the equipment follows the site, and buying software or a megaphone cannot replace qualification and training.

Organisation｜There are different arrangements such as a venue or a travel agency. Establish who is responsible for the assignment, the opening updates and the visitor questions, and do not assume you can take on business independently just because you know the route.

Scheduling and physical demands｜The combined United States material describes part-time, seasonal and weekend, evening and holiday work and long periods of walking and standing. The specific Chinese scheduling, preparation time and pay need separate checking.

Cooperation｜Explain the confirmed material, the change times and the unresolved questions to the corresponding colleagues; do not replace the venue status or the travel agency's arrangements with a verbal guess.

Re-checking and reporting｜The feedback must state the target of the change, the basis and the confirming person, and keep the current route and material version; real emergencies are handled under the unit's and the relevant authorities' requirements.

Observable quality｜Accurate facts, clear expression, responding to needs and adjusting to conditions can serve as self-check signals. A paper experience does not declare professional acceptance, and real tasks still require training and feedback.

Tour guides and escorts provide visit guidance and location commentary for individuals or groups, prepare material and routes, respond to questions, and observe visitor activity and on-site limits. The United States identity uses O*NET 39-7011.00; actual tour guide activity in China requires separate checking of the qualification, the tour guide certificate and the travel agency assignment, and a venue commentary role cannot be judged by the Chinese title alone. You can start with the fictional in-museum material on this page to complete the paper experience of checking the commentary and arranging the time.

Managing facilities, budgets, staff scheduling and leisure services. It takes on operations and personnel management, while a tour guide focuses on visitor reception, commentary and the set itinerary.

Arranging the event budget, venue, suppliers and services around the client's objectives. The planner coordinates the event resources and contracts; the tour guide delivers the confirmed visit and explanation.

Explaining natural and historical resources through park tours and educational activities. It overlaps with guiding but requires added knowledge of park resources, nature education and protection rules.

Studying historical archives, evaluating material and producing research, publication or exhibition output. The research method and the responsibility for evidence go beyond reciting a piece of commentary and require independent historical source training.
Venue and historical site tours
Explaining exhibits, sites and visit rules to visitors, answering questions and controlling the pace of the visit.
A common tour setting in this occupation; the material must be confirmed and unknown dates and names must not be fabricated.
Being willing to verify material and to explain professional content to visitors from different backgrounds.
City sightseeing and group escort
Escorting visitors to the set locations, explaining the route, the assembly and the changes, and helping visitors follow the rules.
Group movement and on-site coordination stand out; transport, routes and the travel agency assignment still follow the real arrangements.
Liking contact with crowds and being able to accept walking, repeated explanation and itinerary changes.
Entertainment and recreation managers (except gambling)
Taking on operations and personnel management, while a tour guide focuses on visitor reception, commentary and the set itinerary.
If you would rather organise the whole service team, do a budget and scheduling case first.
Meeting, convention and event planners
The planner coordinates the event resources and contracts; the tour guide delivers the confirmed visit and explanation.
If you like event preparation, verify the supplier comparison and event planning ability first.
Park naturalists
It overlaps with guiding but requires added knowledge of park resources, nature education and protection rules.
If you prefer nature education, check the target park's resources and course requirements first.
Historians
The research method and the responsibility for evidence go beyond reciting a piece of commentary and require independent historical source training.
If you prefer long-term research, complete a source and argumentation exercise first.
How do you choose between venue tours, group escort and the adjacent occupations?

First compare the output you want to complete. Venue commentary and city group escort may both belong to tour guides and escorts; operations management, event planning, nature education and historical research each have their own responsibility. Long-distance travel accommodation and end-to-end logistics are closer to Travel Guides, and the combined United States wage statistic must not turn them all into this page's core duties.

First use the fictional exhibition hall's G1 material card and schedule to verify your interest in explanation and organisation. If you prefer facility operations, event preparation, nature education or historical research, add the ability against the target occupation. Guiding experience helps communication but does not automatically grant management authority, research ability or a specific job qualification.

This occupation uses O*NET 39-7011.00. The four adjacent occupations check the tasks of 11-9072.00, 13-1121.00, 19-1031.03 and 19-3093.00 respectively; the experience suggestions are designed by the author. BLS 39-7010 is a combined scope that includes Travel Guides and is not used as an independent statistic for this occupation.
Once the tour setting you want is determined, distinguish the ability of AI to draft material from on-site judgement, qualifications, assignment and visitor safety responsibility.

You can try turning the location material into a commentary draft, a question list or a route comparison, but this is only an editorial use. The G1 exhibit label and times must be checked by a person item by item, and generating more text does not prove the facts are correct, the expression better or the service already automated.

Venue commentary, route arrangement and on-site response involve different inputs. A draft can check the text, a route needs the real opening status and time slots checked, and on-site work also requires responding to visitors and colleagues; the differences on this page are an editorial summary, and one output cannot be used to infer that the whole job is replaceable.

This round obtained no comparable occupational AI adoption rate or net time saved data for tour guides and escorts. Confirming adoption requires stating the organisation, task, period, tool and material scope; a software list, an occupational task file and a risk framework cannot serve as a national usage survey.

The five steps below are the editorial trial process: clarify the task and the material permission, confirm the limits, then check the facts, the calculations and the opening status, and finally keep the change records. Real service is confirmed by the corresponding organisation and staff, and generated text does not equal assignment, approval or an on-site safety judgement.

A tool also cannot turn an unconfirmed route or fee suggestion into a permitted arrangement.

No. The combined United States material includes customer tips in wages, but China's Tourism Law and tour guide administration measures prohibit asking tourists for tips; a United States pay description does not constitute permission for Chinese conduct, and the service, the charging and the contract must be checked separately.

How will AI affect tour preparation, on-site service and responsibility?

Insufficient evidence: the comparable AI adoption rate, task effects and net employment causal data for this occupation, and the score remains missing. Material summaries, drafts and route comparisons are editorial trial suggestions; the facts, times, visitor information and service responsibility are still checked by people. The combined United States 39-7010 2025—2035 overall growth of 6.3%, the ten-year net increase of about 3,900 and the average annual 11,900 openings including replacements are not independent for this page's sub-category or AI causation.

The five kinds of material respectively support the occupational tasks, the Chinese practice rules, the wage statistics method, the combined employment projection and the voluntary risk method. They are not a tour guide AI effect experiment and do not swap regions, populations or causal conclusions.

The voluntary NIST AI RMF 1.0 risk management method
Editors can use its risk identification and checking ideas to check the material, the output and the re-checking process, without declaring a verified guiding benefit.
Not a tour guide sample, not a mandatory Chinese process, and it provides no adoption or replacement rate for this occupation.
Does generating a commentary script prove that guiding works better?

No. The draft must be traced back to the exhibit label and the location material, then the audience's understanding and feedback must be checked. This page has no empirical effect evidence, and G1 to G3 only observe whether the author can check the facts and adjust the arrangements.
Can a route arranged by a tool be used to take visitors around directly?

It cannot be executed on the strength of a draft alone. Check the real opening status, transport, group needs, risks and authority; G2 is only a fictional confirmed alternative, and an unconfirmed route must not be treated as usable on site.
Can visitor information be uploaded directly in order to optimise the commentary?

The NIST method prompts checking information handling risks; the duty of confidentiality for Chinese visitor information is separately based on the Tourism Law text on this page. Check the required data, the purpose, the recipient and the permission first, and do not assume names, telephone numbers or photographs may be uploaded; the paper experience uses fictional information only.

O*NET only describes the United States 39-7011.00 tasks and does not provide a Chinese practising licence. China's qualification certificate, tour guide certificate and travel agency assignment are based on the Tourism Law and tour guide administration measures texts on this page, and the specific venue role is judged by the actual activity; a tool does not grant a qualification.
What conditions should be checked before a trial?

Clarify the task to be organised, the original material, the material permission and the unknowns, then check the output, the times and the rules manually. Re-check when the conditions change, and do not treat a previously correct draft as permanently valid.

Insufficient evidence: a precise national wage median or percentile for tour guides and escorts in China. The 2025 pre-tax annual average of 79,857 yuan for social production and life service personnel in enterprises above the designated size serves only as a broad background for visitor guidance, commentary and visit service tasks, not an official occupational equivalence, a separately listed tour guide figure or a personal range, and self-employed and freelance workers are excluded. The Chifeng local survey and the Guide County historical recruitment are listed separately and do not fill in the national distribution.

When comparing pay, first list the base wage, the tour allowance, the temporary tour guide service fee, personal social insurance and the costs borne. A travel agency employing a guide must pay the remuneration according to law; for temporary engagement the service fee must be paid in full, and the guide must not be required to advance funds or be charged.

The Chifeng enterprise sample survey reflects the local 2025 annual tour guide wage and cannot be treated as an individual's take-home income or the national entry rate. The Guide County announcement's total monthly wage includes personal social insurance, and the two differ in period, population and unit, so no direct high or low ranking is made.

The verified items are the Chifeng 2025 median annual tour guide wage of 66,100 yuan and the Guide County 2026 historical monthly quote for 1 full-time tour guide (commentator). The two are a local survey and a single recruitment respectively and do not constitute a nationally representative sample.

The Guide County announcement gives a 1-month probation at 2,800 yuan per month, and 3,500 yuan per month including personal social insurance after passing; after 1 continuous year with outstanding performance it may reach 4,000 yuan per month including personal social insurance. Applications closed on June 23, so as at October 1, 2026 it is a historical sample.
Chinese tour guide income: the broad service annual average, the local survey and the historical monthly wage

The historical Guide County role had a probation of 2,800 yuan per month, 3,500 yuan per month after assessment, and 4,000 yuan per month once the conditions of a full continuous year on the job with outstanding results are met; the latter two include personal social insurance costs. The Chifeng 2025 local tour guide annual wage guide rates: low 52,450 yuan, lower quartile 55,237.50 yuan, median 66,100 yuan, upper quartile 70,062.50 yuan and high 70,550 yuan; they do not represent national income, the specific percentiles of the low and high values and the occupational sample size are not disclosed, and they are not merged with the role's monthly quote.

The Guide County 2026 historical quote for a full-time tour guide (commentator): probation of 1 month at 2,800 yuan per month; after passing, a total wage of 3,500 yuan per month including personal social insurance; only after 1 continuous year with outstanding performance may it reach 4,000 yuan per month including personal social insurance. It must not be written as an automatic pay rise or post-tax income.
The median annual tour guide wage of 66,100 yuan from the Chifeng 2025 enterprise sample survey applies to the Chifeng area, and the occupational sample size is not listed separately.

The historical Guide County role recruited 1 person, junior college or above, no major restriction, under 30 years of age, with a tour guide qualification certificate preferred; these are a specific employer's conditions and cannot be explained as a uniform age or education threshold for all tour guides.

China's tour guide qualification examination pass certificate differs from the tour guide certificate. After obtaining the qualification, one must also conclude a labour contract with a travel agency or register with the relevant tourism industry organisation, then apply for the tour guide certificate according to law; carrying out tour guide activity requires accepting an assignment from a travel agency as prescribed.

A local survey and one historical role are not enough to derive a national wage. Exchange rate conversion, the tourism industry average wage or an individual peak-season quote cannot be used to fill in this occupation's national gap.

Weekends, public holidays and seasonality may affect scheduling and paid opportunities. Write the confirmed labour contract, allowance and service fee conditions clearly, and do not assume a tour every day or multiply one tour's pay by the days of the year.

Insufficient evidence: the causal effect of Chinese tour guide AI adoption on wages. Drafting material and the risk method cannot prove net time saved or income change; the 79,857 yuan broad service annual average, the Chifeng local survey and the Guide County historical quote are not AI effect studies, and the actual task adjustment, review, visitor flow and contractual pay are checked separately.

The 79,857 yuan is the 2025 pre-tax annual average for broad service roles in enterprises above the designated size, not a separately listed tour guide median, percentile or starting-pay personal range, and self-employed and freelance workers are excluded. The Chifeng 2025 local tour guide survey and the closed Guide County 2026 historical monthly wage are listed separately; an unknown tax basis is not filled in, and a preferred qualification does not exempt the tour guide certificate and assignment. The combined United States 39-7010 statistic is not converted into Chinese income.

The United States May 2025 wage belongs to the combined Tour and Travel Guides statistic 39-7010, which includes this page's 39-7011.00 and Travel Guides. The median annual wage is 38,120 US dollars and cannot be called an independent median for this occupation or an individual's post-tax receipts.
The combined occupational annual wage P10 is 28,520 US dollars, indicating a lower position in the distribution; it is not a guaranteed wage for newcomers and does not represent Chinese job pay.

The combined occupational annual wage P90 is 60,930 US dollars, indicating the threshold of a higher position in the distribution; individual income or stable full-year work cannot be promised from it.

Combined occupational employment in 2025–2035 is projected from 62,200 to 66,100, growth of 6.3% and a net increase of about 3,900. The average of 11,900 openings a year also includes replacements after leaving or changing roles and cannot be treated as annual net growth.

OEWS wages exclude the self-employed; the EP employment projection includes them, at a 2025 self-employment share of 9.2%. Wages and employment must not be multiplied together to estimate the whole occupation's income.

The official annual wage statistic is compiled using an annual hours method; full-time full-year usually uses the 2,080-hour basis. Even where an annual wage is provided, it does not mean a seasonal or part-time guide actually has 2,080 paid hours in the year.

The combined occupation's P50 is 38,120 US dollars per year. A percentile is a statistical position, not a seniority grade, a take-home amount or a guarantee of an individual's full-year income.

P10/P25/P50/P75/P90 are 28,520, 32,910, 38,120, 47,700 and 60,930 US dollars per year respectively, all United States combined statistics including Travel Guides and not corresponding to entry, intermediate or senior qualifications.

description.text: Tour guides and escorts provide visit guidance and location commentary for individuals or groups, prepare material and routes, respond to questions, and observe visitor activity and on-site limits. The United States identity uses O*NET 39-7011.00; actual tour guide activity in China requires separate checking of the qualification, the tour guide certificate and the travel agency assignment, and a venue commentary role cannot be judged by the Chinese title alone. You can start with the fictional in-museum material on this page to complete the paper experience of checking the commentary and arranging the time.
